answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by withholding payout weight until an identity has climbed a public reputation ridge of independently reproduced work. Each newcomer keeps a bound diary of recent transactions; established miners re-execute a random sample and countersign only when the trail matches. That countersignature is the signal that unlocks mining and grading rights. A fable of cheap cloned names then fails, because the diary and countersignatures are non-transferable: every extra identity must earn a fresh trail, and farming those signatures costs more than the extra rewards.
